agent-automations.descriptionHTML:
Note

This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Lists automations created by the authenticated user across repositories they can read. This includes both personal and shared automations created by the caller, but excludes shared automations created by another user.

Use the repository-scoped list operation for those automations. The type filter only narrows this creator-scoped collection.

To call this endpoint, OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

  • the repo scope for private or internal repositories
  • the repo scope or public_repo scope for public repositories

Fine-grained access tokens for "List automations for user"

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

  • GitHub App user access tokens
  • Fine-grained personal access tokens

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

  • "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read)

GitHub App installation access tokens are not supported for this endpoint.

Use the type field to distinguish personal and shared automations.

  • the repo scope for private or internal repositories
  • the repo scope or public_repo scope for public repositories

Fine-grained access tokens for "List automations for a repository"

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

  • GitHub App user access tokens
  • GitHub App installation access tokens
  • Fine-grained personal access tokens

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

  • "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read)

agent-automations.descriptionHTML:
Note

This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Creates a new automation in a repository. Personal automations are private to their creator. Shared automations are visible to anyone with read access to the repository and manageable by anyone with write access to the repository.

GitHub App installation access tokens can create shared automations by setting type to shared. The installation must belong to the repository owner and the token must have "Agent tasks" repository permissions (write). Personal automations require a user token. For installation tokens, created_by identifies the App's bot account.

To call this endpoint, you must have write access to the repository and the "Allow automations" setting must be enabled for the repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

  • the repo scope for private or internal repositories
  • the repo scope or public_repo scope for public repositories

Fine-grained access tokens for "Create an automation for a repository"

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

  • GitHub App user access tokens
  • GitHub App installation access tokens
  • Fine-grained personal access tokens

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

  • "Agent tasks" repository permissions (write)

agent-automations.descriptionHTML:
Note

This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Lists available tools for automations in a repository, including both GitHub-provided tools and tools provided by custom MCP servers.

GitHub-provided tools are returned in named groups, with a name and description provided for each tool.

MCP entries describe configured tool selection, not live discovery or runtime availability. An explicit allowlist is returned in tools, with each id in <server-name>/<tool-name> format, for example sentry/list_issues. An allowlist of ["*"] is returned as supports_wildcard: true with an empty tools array. Server URLs, authentication headers, environment variables, and credentials are never returned.

For MCP tools, a list of configured MCP servers is provided, along with the tools allowlisted for each server. Where supports_wildcard is true, any tool that exists on the server can be used.

GitHub App installation access tokens can list available automation tools. The installation must belong to the repository owner and the token must have "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read).

To call this endpoint, OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

  • the repo scope for private or internal repositories
  • the repo scope or public_repo scope for public repositories

Fine-grained access tokens for "List available automation tools for a repository"

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

  • GitHub App user access tokens
  • GitHub App installation access tokens
  • Fine-grained personal access tokens

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

  • "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read)

agent-automations.descriptionHTML:
Note

This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Updates an existing automation in a repository. The automation must be a personal automation belonging to you or a shared automation. Omitted fields are left unchanged. The automation's type is immutable.

GitHub App installation access tokens can update shared automations. The installation must belong to the repository owner and the token must have "Agent tasks" repository permissions (write). Personal automations require a user token.

To call this endpoint, you must have write access to the repository and the "Allow automations" setting must be enabled for the repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

  • the repo scope for private or internal repositories
  • the repo scope or public_repo scope for public repositories

Fine-grained access tokens for "Update an automation"

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

  • GitHub App user access tokens
  • GitHub App installation access tokens
  • Fine-grained personal access tokens

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

  • "Agent tasks" repository permissions (write)

type.description: The type of automation. `personal` keeps it private to its creator and its runs act as that user. `shared` makes it belong to the repository, visible to anyone with read access to the repository, and its runs act as the Copilot app rather than as a person.

require_actor_write_permission.description: When true, event-triggered runs require the event actor to have repo write permission, even when the org's allow_read_access_triggers policy is enabled. Does not apply to interval-scheduled runs, which always run as the automation owner.

continuous_history.description: When true, runs of this automation build on the session history of its previous runs, and runs of the same automation are serialized. Not tracked in revision history.

cadence.description: One or more schedules on which the Automation runs.

hour_utc.description: UTC hour anchor (0 through 23) for daily and weekly schedules. Omitted daily and weekly values default to `0` (midnight UTC).

day_of_week.description: UTC weekday anchor for weekly schedules, where `0` is Sunday and `6` is Saturday. Omitted weekly values default to Monday (`1`).

minute_utc.description: UTC minute anchor for daily and weekly schedules. Omitted daily and weekly values default to `0`. Must be omitted whenever `cadence` includes `hourly`.

write_scope.description: Has no effect: scheduled runs can change any resource in the repository, and an organization or repository policy requiring trigger-scoped writes does not apply to them.

Note

This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Deletes an automation in a repository. The automation must be a personal automation belonging to you or a shared automation.

GitHub App installation access tokens can delete shared automations. The installation must belong to the repository owner and the token must have "Agent tasks" repository permissions (write). Personal automations require a user token.

To call this endpoint, you must have write access to the repository and the "Allow automations" setting must be enabled for the repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

  • the repo scope for private or internal repositories
  • the repo scope or public_repo scope for public repositories

  • GitHub App installation access tokens
  • Fine-grained personal access tokens

agent-automations.descriptionHTML:
Note

This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Returns a paginated list of tasks created by an automation in the specified repository. The automation must belong to that exact repository.

User-owned automation history is visible only to the automation's creator. Repository-owned automation history is visible to callers with read access to repository automations. Deleted and unlisted tasks are excluded. Tasks produced by private-session agents are excluded unless the caller created the task, is a task collaborator, or the task is shared.

A missing repository, an inaccessible repository, or an automation that does not belong to the specified repository returns 404 without revealing which condition occurred.

GitHub App installation access tokens can list tasks for shared automations. The installation must belong to the repository owner and the token must have "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read). Personal automations require a user token.

Fine-grained access tokens for "List tasks for an automation in a repository"

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

  • GitHub App user access tokens
  • GitHub App installation access tokens
  • Fine-grained personal access tokens

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

  • "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read)

agent-automations.descriptionHTML:
Note

This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Runs an automation in a repository. Set event to manual and optionally include context of up to 10,000 characters, which will be injected into the automation's prompt.

The repository must have the "Allow automations" setting enabled, and the automation must be a personal automation belonging to you or a shared automation.

GitHub App installation access tokens can run shared automations. The installation must belong to the repository owner and the token must have "Agent tasks" repository permissions (write). Personal automations require a user token.

A successful response accepts the run request and includes a preallocated task_id, which can be fetched with the "Get a task by repo" Agent tasks API. It does not confirm execution or task creation. Task creation is asynchronous, so fetching the task immediately may return 404 Not Found, and downstream skips or failures can prevent its creation.

To call this endpoint, you must have write access to the repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

  • the repo scope for private or internal repositories
  • the repo scope or public_repo scope for public repositories

Fine-grained access tokens for "Run an automation"

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

  • GitHub App user access tokens
  • GitHub App installation access tokens
  • Fine-grained personal access tokens

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

  • "Agent tasks" repository permissions (write)
